Long English-only stretches (meta talk about the recorder 03:40-05:52; verb-pair explanation 17:06-18:06; usage discussion 46:08-48:13; causative-verb wrap-up 57:27-1:02:40). Latin transliteration on Medi's lines at 06:38-06:47 (date), 07:08-07:20 (clock), 19:39 (means ajik), 30:49 (albo), 48:20-48:31. ASR-garbled Amal fixes: 12:13 'بدائية' (read as وردية), 13:42 'فعلاً' (read as فعلين), 38:33 'أشياءي نوع الإل' (unreadable; Medi says he did not say ال - no row), 45:57 'بتنكسر'. Not written (S4/S5/self-fix): 03:11 جهزت->وجهّزت (shadda F3, twice), 05:58 الأربعاء->الخميس self-fix, 06:40 date order self-fix before her عشرة تسعة, 07:46 قربان for خربان (ق/خ), 15:02 أزعشتك (ش/ج), 20:57 متأكتي, 29:46 سكرتي self-fix, 33:41 سهوني (ص/س), 34:14 يسكر->اكسر self-fix (her 'K before S' = letter order), 35:17 كنا self-fix, 42:53-43:16 انكسرت letter-order fix, 52:52 اشي->إشي vowel, 44:18 اثنعش accepted as ممتاز. 'air conditioning' is used in English by both (07:39, 12:53, 48:29, 53:14) and is not on her sheet, so not tier 3. 09:13 'مهندس كهربجي' (redundant pairing) got an explanation, not a fix - no row. Medi turns counted = Medi lines containing Arabic script (366 of 615 Medi lines).
coverage.r2: Whole file read in order. Left out as S4 pronunciation: وجهّزت shadda 03:13, صلاحتو→صلحته 08:11 (vowel length), قربان for خربان 07:46, أزعشتك 15:02, سكرتي/سهوني/يسكر letter-order slips 29:46/33:41/34:14 ('The K is before the S'), إن كسر→انكسر spacing 49:31, إيدها انكسرت letter order 43:10, ولا اشي→إشي vowel 52:52, بعيم for بقيم 27:05, بفزت for ببسّط 56:04, تباين for تبعي 48:31. Three letter-order slips that produced real other words (زعمت, بخسر, تعبي) ARE written as low-confidence vocab rows because Amal treated them as words and Medi asked (04:05) that such fixes be marked. Latin-transliterated stretch 06:38-07:20 (date and clock). Garbled/unreadable Medi lines not judged: 19:36-19:39 (مين أزعجك), 19:54 أشيك تير, 24:50 بتدايك, 30:02-30:21 (we broke your windows), 38:33 Amal 'أشياءي نوع الإل' (unclear, he says he did not say el-), 42:05-42:15 (hand), 54:24 إمّني, 55:05 أبن كتير, 55:30 بفيت, 55:33 Amal 'أنا واعي'. English-only stretches: 03:40-05:51 (recording rules), 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:13, 57:37-1:01:49 (causative verbs). Drill slips during conjugation runs (45:24 بينكسري, 45:34) and self-fixes (13:37, 29:46, 34:20, 05:58) not written. Amal used English 'air conditioning' herself (48:29) and مكيف is not on her sheet, so his 'air conditioning' is not tier 3; YouTube, bones not on sheet.

r3_note: Transcript notes for the merger: several of Amal's fixes are garbled by ASR and I read them from structure, not spelling - 12:13 'بدائية' (= وردية), 13:42 'بس فعلاً' (= بس فعلين), 45:57 'بتنكسر' (probably her feeding بننكسر). 06:38-07:20 is Latin-transliterated (date, clock). Medi's ق comes out as ء/nothing throughout (أزد = قصد, بعيم = بقيم) - S4, not vocab. D19 and D26 were the same الفعلات slip split by the matcher; D26 carries the row, D19 drops r2's separate 'verbs' half. D1 and D2 were the same جو/الجو slip; D1 carries the row. D24's row is re-anchored from r2's 12:14 echo to the real slip at 12:06 (ورداني); if an agreed row already sits at 12:06 it is a duplicate. I did not open the readers' JSON or compare.json, so 'added' is empty - the explicit 10:34-11:07 صلح→ساعد fix (Amal 11:02 'You said صلح which is fix... he helped me?') is almost certainly an agreed row; if it is not, it is a vocab-A tier 1 recast worth adding.

rows.why: He asked how the bride (عروس) was, meaning the wedding; she recast عرس and he repeated عروس again at 01:57.

Letter-order slip that lands on a different real verb (زعم = claimed) for عزمت (sheet: 'i invited | Ana 3azamet | أنا عزمت'); she recast it and Medi himself at 04:05 asked that it be marked wrong - borderline S4 root-letter slip.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: Clock time: he said talaat (three, masc/short form) for the time; she asked three or two, he fixed to intayn and she recast الساعة تنتين إلا تلت (feminine number after el-saa3a).

Answering her كيف الجو عندكم اليوم he said جو كتير كتير: 'the weather' is a known thing and takes el- (her prompt and the sheet row 'it's hot | El-jaw shoab | الجو شوب' both have الجو). The adjective شوب is absent in the transcript but she answered عن جد؟ as if she heard a complete statement, so the missing word is likely an ASR drop and is not scored - only the el- is. B reading.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same moment; the transcript proves only the missing el- (جو without ال), so the final row is r2's A1 grammar-B, not r1's vocab-B 'missing شوب', which cannot be verified (possible ASR drop, no signal from her).

rows.why: رن takes على (sheet: i call | Ana barenn (3ala) | أنا برن); he used لـ and she let it pass - he then got lost hunting for 'electricity' and she followed that (08:51). B reading.
rows.r3_why: Real let-pass: the transcript shows لمهندس clearly and her own sheet fixes the preposition as على.

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word for electricity and she supplied كهربا (sheet: 'electricity | Kahraba | كهربا').

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: Profession idafa: the second noun takes el- (مهندس الكهربا); he left it bare and she recast.

rows.amal_said: Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
rows.why: Didn't-know: after his مهندس كهرباء she volunteered the everyday word كهربجي, which he had never attempted; he repeated it at 09:13 (and as كراجي at 09:30 / 09:39, pronunciation). Not on her sheet - he says so himself at 09:39 - so it is a new-word row, tier 0.
rows.r3_why: A new word she taught that he never attempted is a didn't-know per the brief: vocab-A, tier 0, signal asked.

rows.medi_said: I think is كراجي electrician, and then electrical engineering is...
rows.why: He turned her كهربجي into كراجي (a different word, garage/mechanic) and repeated it at 09:39 and 09:48; she recast كهربجي.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس، uh, مهندس.
rows.why: Saying who the man he called is - 'he is not a kahrabji, he is an engineer' - is a present noun predicate: Levantine negates it with مش and no 'to be' (C4); ما يكون is neither that nor a licensed ykoon context (B8: only after lamma/iza or for habits). The man's job is a present fact, so ما كان (r2) is not the target either. She said nothing about it; her 10:30 صلح لي moves to his next clause.
rows.english: He isn't an electrician, he's an engineer.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the slip; the transcript supports C4 (noun predicate negated with a verb form) over B6 (the identity claim is present, not past); B8 goes in bucket2 for the stray ykoon.

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلّح (fix) for 'help'; she asked whether he meant helped and he produced ساعدني (sheet: 'help | Saa3ed | ساعد'), which she confirmed at 11:10.
'For me' rides on the preposition (لي), not as an object ending on the verb (صلحني = he fixed me, 10:44); she separated the two forms.
rows.english: He fixed (it) for me a bit

rows.why: Masculine colour adjective after the feminine noun بلوزة; her recast is transcribed as بدائية (almost certainly وردية) and she said صح when he repeated the feminine form at 12:14.

بلوزة is feminine, so 'pink' must be وردية; he said the masculine ورداني. Her 12:13 line (transcribed بدائية, an ASR shape of وردية) is the recast - his 'وردنية that's right' at 12:14 accepts it and her 12:16 صح confirms his echo. The extra ن in his echo وردنية (r2's wrong piece) is S4, so the row is anchored on the real slip ورداني. Her sheet has pink as زهري, but she accepted وردي here.
rows.r3_why: r2's 12:14 وردنية is his echo of her fix (she said صح), so that piece alone is pronunciation; the underlying slip the transcript supports is 12:06 ورداني (masc adjective on a feminine noun) with her 12:13 recast - kept as grammar A8. If an agreed row already covers 12:06, this is its duplicate.

rows.why: Wrong form of the verb 'stayed' (sheet: 'i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | أنا ضليت'); she did not understand ('what?') and supplied ضليت. Could also be read as B5 past ending.

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.
rows.why: He said 'stayed my house' with no preposition; she prompted 'bi or fi?' and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50.

Explaining why he stayed home today (اليوم ضليت بي بيتي): 'because there is AC' - existence in the plain present is في / عندي, not يكون (B8: ykoon only after lamma/iza or for habits; C1: no 'to be' in the present). She moved on to شو بتتذكر at 13:04 without a fix. 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet, so the English word itself is not an error. B reading.
rows.english: because there is air conditioning (at home)
rows.r3_why: Real let-pass: عشان يكون AC is not how a native states that the AC is there; kept as grammar-B, low because his intent (cause vs purpose) is not spelled out.

rows.why: 'One word': the modifier وحدة sits after the noun like an adjective; he put it first (English order) and she recast noun-first, بس كلمة وحدة. A7 is the rule broken (modifier after the noun); E1 is the secondary tag because the modifier is the number one.
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree on the slip; the transcript shows a word-order fix, which is A7's rule (E1 only covers the form of the noun after 2 / 3-10 / 11+), so A7 with E1 as bucket2.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: 'Two verbs' takes the dual فعلين, not فعل + تنين (E1: 2 has its own form). Her reply mirrors his phrase (أههم بس فعل-) and 'فعلاً' ('indeed') makes no sense after أههم بس, so it is almost certainly فعلين mis-transcribed - filed as her recast. Medium because the transcript does not show the ين.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the slip; the transcript's structure (her أههم بس فعل- right after his بس فعل تنين) supports a recast rather than a let-pass, so kind = grammar with signal recast, medium confidence for the garbled ending.

rows.why: Drill 'you got annoyed with me': after انزعجتي he started ما (reaching for 'with me'); she asked ليش ما؟, he answered 'You said with by me... مني، مني sorry' (16:10) and gave انزعجتي مني at 16:22 ('Perfect'). انزعج takes من (her 14:35: 'annoyed with you you would say مِنْ'). Medium: his ما may partly be a stutter of ماضي, but her question and his fix show she heard a wrong preposition.
rows.r3_why: Real prompt-then-fix: her ليش ما؟ and his correction to مني are both in the transcript; D2 (verb + its fixed preposition).

rows.amal_said: بتحب نشوف الواجب أو الفعل اللي بعده؟
rows.why: He asks her to repeat; كم مرة = how many times. Sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة. She just rephrased her question.
English calque 'one more' with أكتر; she recast كمان واحد (sheet: 'also / more / too | Kamaan | كمان').
Masculine participle for a female addressee; she asked 'inti or inta?' and he fixed to مزعوجة at 18:54.

rows.medi_said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.
rows.why: Plural subject 'many things' needs the plural verb بزعجوني; he used the singular; she recast twice and he acknowledged 'it's plural'.
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days

rows.why: Same plural-agreement slip repeated on his second attempt; she recast بزعجوني and he fixed at 20:33.
'These days' needs the plural أيام; he used the singular اليوم and she recast.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: The noun after هدول keeps its el-; he dropped it in the fixed version and she moved on (طيب).
'Are you sure THAT you didn't annoy him' needs إنو; he used اللي. She asked 'why illi?' (21:27) and said إنو مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you (pl) didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'you (pl) didn't annoy HIM' is missing the object ending -ه on the verb; she moved to the illi problem and let this pass.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا ما she keeps the b- (إذا ما بشوف); he used the bare أشوفك; he repeated her form at 22:31. Her ruling here differs from the plain B3 drop, so filed under B3 as her exception.
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.why: Negative command: he gave the positive imperative إنزعجي for 'don't be annoyed'; she prompted 'so don't be', he produced ما تنزعج (23:24) then ما تنزعجي (23:32) after her echo.
'With them' is the ending on the preposition (منهم), not a separate pronoun; she had said بعدين and let it pass.
After مش قصدهم ('they didn't mean to') the verb drops its b-: يدايقوكي; he kept the b- and insisted 'أنا بعرف هيك' at 25:16. Pronouncing دايق as تاي is S4, not counted.
rows.english: They didn't mean to upset you

rows.why: Second use of كم مرة (how many times) to ask her to repeat; sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة. She just repeated herself.

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: 'I add' (sheet: i add | Bazeed | بزيد): he produced بزياد, a wrong vowel mould of a verb he knows (the ī became yā - a different shape, not a length slip); she recast بزيد and he repeated it at 26:42.
rows.r3_why: Real: a committed wrong form of a sheet verb, recast by her and echoed back; tier 2 (wrong form of a known word), medium because the first fragment بزيء shows he was still searching.

rows.why: Groping for 'I remove' he produced only fragments (شول may be the start of بشيل, which would also be usable), never a committed wrong word; she supplied بقيم (sheet: i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم), so this is a didn't-know (tier 0), not a tier-1 wrong word. His later بعينك / بعين / بعيم are بقيم with a dropped ق (S4).
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the moment; the transcript shows search fragments, not a wrong lexical item, so tier 0 / asked (r2) over tier 1 (r1).

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el- (أول الفعل / أول الكلمة); he put el- on both. She let it pass.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / of the word

rows.why: بخسر is a different verb (I lose) for بكسر 'I break' (sheet: 'i break | Ana bakser | أنا بكسر'); she said 'close' and recast; he still said بخسر at 28:06-28:26 before switching. Could be argued as a خ/ك sound slip (S4).
3pl past needs -u (كسروا); he gave كسرت; her echo prompted him and he fixed at 28:47, confirmed 28:53.
In the present-tense drill (هم ...) he dropped the b-: يكسروا for بيكسروا; she let it pass.

'You keep breaking my plates': after إنتِ بتظلي the verb needs the you-f prefix بت- (بتكسري). His production is transcribed only as the tail زري and she said she did not hear the t, i.e. the person marker was missing; he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31. Low: the transcript holds only a fragment, so whether he said بكسري (B18) or كسري (B1) cannot be shown.
rows.r3_why: Real prompt-then-fix (her 'I didn't hear the t' + his بتكسري), but his line is a fragment, so kept at low confidence; the missing piece she named is the person marker, hence B18 with B1 second.

rows.why: MSA 2pl past ending -تم instead of Levantine -توا; she let it pass in the conjugation run.
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used the singular كاسته; she recast كساته.

For 'his cup' she recast كاسه; his كاسته keeps the -t- of كاسة before the possessive (sheet has 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'), which is normally fine, so low - the transcript may have dropped her vowel (كاستو).
كاسة is feminine so the verb is انكسرت; he used the masculine; she recast and confirmed 'because it's female' at 41:00.
The subject is عمر (masc), so كان, not كانت, even though it is 'her' age; he pushed for كانت twice (43:36, 43:43) and she said لأ.
He said eleven for twelve (sheet: 'eleven | e7da3sh | إحداعش', 'twelve | tna3sh | تنعش'); she said 12 and إتناش (43:55).
Feminine form invented for the noun he knows (sheet: 'present tense | Mudaare3 | مضارع'); she recast مضارع; he still said المضارعة at 44:41.

Conjugating انكسر for هو/هي he produced بينكسري (masc بي- prefix + fem -ي ending), a form that exists for no subject; she did not fix it, she redirected him to the skipped إنتو. Low: he was switching subjects mid-word. Her هو at 45:38 fixes a different slip (هي بينكسر).
rows.r3_why: Real let-pass of a non-existent form; kept low because it sits inside a subject switch and she steered away rather than reacting to it.

rows.why: إحنا of the un-verb انكسر is بننكسر (b-n-nkasir); he gave بنكسر, which is the إحنا form of plain كسر ('we break'), and she went straight into usage talk (46:08). Low: ASR may have collapsed the double ن, and her 45:57 line (transcribed بتنكسر) may itself have been her feeding him بننكسر.
rows.r3_why: Kept as a low-confidence let-pass: the transcript shows بنكسر after a hesitation, but a merged double ن in ASR is plausible, so the merger should weigh it lightly.

rows.medi_said: Do I say for air condition?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'my AC' and she supplied the الـ X تبعي construction (AC is not on her sheet and she keeps it in English); tier 0 keeps it apart from slips. His echo تباين (48:31) is pronunciation.
rows.r3_why: A 'how do you say X' answered by her is a didn't-know per the brief: vocab-A, tier 0, signal asked.

rows.amal_said: انكسر. Did it actually like break?
rows.why: انكسر is for physically shattering; for the AC 'stopped working' she wants خرب/خربان (49:05, 49:51 'my issue is with the verb itself... It's physical'); he conceded at 50:05.
rows.english: The AC broke (stopped working) from the heat

rows.why: 'I never broke anything' is past; he used present because he thought أبداً forces present; she asked بكسر أو كسرت, he fixed to ما كسرت (52:36) and she confirmed كسرت.

rows.amal_said: it? Do you wanna say because the, the air conditioning tired me?
rows.why: Letter-order slip turns تبعي (mine) into تعّبي ('tired me'); she read it as 'tired me out' and asked; he rephrased without it at 53:29. Borderline S4 but it changed the meaning and she flagged it.
Negate the verb with ما (ما نمت منيح), not مش before the adverb; she recast and he repeated at 53:54.

rows.medi_said: إن و-- إن. الف-الفعلات. الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Plural of فعل (sheet: verb – verbs | Fe3el | فعل) is the broken plural أفعال; he invented a -ات plural فعلات, she recast أفعال and he said الأفعال at 54:53. The reader brief files an invented plural pattern as vocab tier 2; A9 is the grammar mould it belongs to, should the tally want a bucket2.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the slip and only the label differs; the reader brief explicitly lists 'wrong plural pattern he invented' under vocab tier 2, so vocab-A tier 2 (r1) over grammar A9 (r2).

rows.why: 'I am annoyed' is the passive participle مزعوج; مزعج = annoying (both on her sheet as separate rows); she recast and asked what أنا مزعج means (56:52).

rows.medi_said: is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
rows.why: Naming the verb pair he gave the bare أكسر; she recast بكسر and بنكسر.

Replying to her يلا بشوفك ('see you') the transcript has ما شوفتك, a negated past ('I didn't see you') where the present b-verb بشوفك / منشوفك is the set reply (B1; B5 second for the tense). She just said باي. Low: very likely an ASR rendering of منشوفك (m-n-shoofak), so the merger may treat it as a transcript hole.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw it and the transcript literally shows ما شوفتك, so it is kept as a low-confidence let-pass; the rule broken, if he said it, is the present b-verb replaced by a negated past (B1 + B5), not C4 (ما before a verb is correct).
